newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa mulls Internet cargo bookings.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa mulls Internet cargo bookings.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it is considering publishing net rates and starting direct cargo bookings on its Internet home page next year.
Michael Kraus, LCAG business development and global accounts manager, told Reuters direct cargo bookings would be open both to forwarders and air cargo shippers.
Price information would have to be added to the system before reservations were added, he said.
"I have nothing against the client knowing what the price is," he said at a presentation of the Lufthansa Cargo Internet site.
Transparent prices would allow clients and forwarders to deal openly about the quality of services, and clients understood forwarders were entitled to commission payments, he added.
But he stressed: "I do not believe clients will try to make bookings through the Internet."
Lufthansa had to be present in the medium, however, which was already widely used by the integrators, he added.
A selling option will not be opened until a so-called "firewall" security system to stop hackers has been solved, he said.
The Lufthansa Cargo Internet World Wide Web site currently offers information on schedules and routes, products and services, and an electronic mail communications option.
Clients and forwarders can also track and trace cargo consignments through a hyper-link to the Traxon cargo reservations system.
LCAG marketing communications manager Michael Zengerle said about 5,000 contacts had been registered since the page was opened two months ago.
Both the German and English language versions were equally popular, implying many international clients were using the service, which also has some French and Italian pages, he said.
